sources.title: Impact of Climate Change on Tropical Cyclones Over Vanuatu: A Case for Informing Disaster Planning and Adaptation Strategies
sources.organization: Krishneel K. Sharma, Savin S. Chand and Soubhik Biswas, Federation University
sources.temporal_coverage: Observed cyclone tracks 1971–2021; CMIP5 future-climate comparisons 2071–2100 versus 1971–2000 under RCP8.5.
sources.methodology: Analyzes SPEArTC cyclone tracks and calibrated CMIP5 simulations using a 500-km buffer for provincial estimates.
sources.limitations: Province-level cyclone proximity is not a direct-landfall count. Future projections use CMIP5 RCP8.5 and model-dependent estimates.

sources.title: As the water flows – remote communities in Vanuatu creating pathways to climate resilience
sources.organization: United Nations Development Programme, Pacific Office
sources.temporal_coverage: Community consultations, project design and reported implementation status through March 2025.
sources.methodology: UNDP project case account drawing on statements from Vanuatu government officials and community participants.
sources.limitations: Not an independent impact evaluation; the project was not yet reported as delivering operating household water service.

sources.title: National Policy on Climate Change and Disaster-Induced Displacement
sources.organization: Government of Vanuatu, National Advisory Board on Climate Change and Disaster Risk Reduction
sources.temporal_coverage: National displacement policy and conditions described in the 2018 document, including 2018 relocation activity.
sources.methodology: National policy framework informed by stakeholder consultations and inter-agency planning.
sources.limitations: Policy describes risks and intended safeguards, not a current implementation review; pathway statements are conditional and multi-causal.

sources.title: Ministry of Climate Change Annual Report 2024
sources.organization: Government of Vanuatu, Ministry of Climate Change
sources.temporal_coverage: Ministry activities, project progress and constraints reported for calendar year 2024, mostly as of 31 December 2024.
sources.methodology: Government ministry annual administrative and project-progress reporting.
sources.limitations: Self-reported progress; several items are procurement, plans or targets rather than independently verified service outcomes.

sources.title: Climate-related disasters and temperature extremes are not associated with conflict risk in Pacific Island countries
sources.organization: Tobias Ide, Ore Koren and Luke Derrick, Environment and Security
sources.temporal_coverage: Geocoded social-conflict and climate analysis for 2012–2020 in three Pacific Island countries.
sources.methodology: Peer-reviewed panel analysis uses 0.5-degree grid-cell-year units, geocoded social conflict events and climate-disaster data.
sources.limitations: Results are pooled across three countries; the study cannot test proposed mediating pathways and does not cover all precipitation or slow-onset effects.

claims.locator: Section 4.1.1, ‘Current Tropical Cyclone Climatology at the Provincial Level’, Figure 3 and accompanying text.
claims.paraphrase: During 1971–2021, the study counted 2.31 cyclone tracks per season within 500 km of Torba, 2.30 of Sanma and 2.45 of Penama.
claims.limitations: The 500-km buffer measures nearby cyclone tracks, not direct landfalls or damage within each province.

claims.locator: Section 4.1.1, Figure 3 and provincial discussion of 1971–1995 versus 1996–2021.
claims.paraphrase: The severe-cyclone share rose in all six provinces; mean wind-speed increases were significant for Tafea (18.1%), Penama (13.4%) and Shefa (13.0%).
claims.limitations: The comparison covers two 26-year periods; significance varies by province, and the study does not estimate resulting local losses.

claims.locator: Section 4.3.2, ‘Multimodel Averages at the Provincial Level’, Table 4 and accompanying text.
claims.paraphrase: Under CMIP5 RCP8.5, the illustrative severe-cyclone intensity of Pam has a shorter projected return period in 2071–2100 than 1971–2000: 77 to 62 years in Torba and 68 to 51 in Penama.
claims.scenario: CMIP5 RCP8.5 high-emissions pathway; 2071–2100 compared with 1971–2000.
claims.limitations: These are modeled return periods for a historical cyclone intensity, not forecasts of Pam recurring or a damage estimate.

claims.locator: Publisher body, opening paragraphs describing Tongariki and Buninga in Shefa Province.
claims.paraphrase: The UNDP account attributes clean-water difficulty on Tongariki and Buninga to saltwater intrusion from rising seas; the boat-accessible islands lack natural streams and rely on rainwater.
claims.limitations: UNDP's case account states the attribution but supplies no local salinity measurements or independent hydrological assessment.

claims.locator: Publisher body, paragraph describing residents' water collection burden.
claims.paraphrase: Residents walk long distances in intense heat carrying water containers that can exceed 20 kg; the account says this is especially treacherous for older people and people with disabilities.
claims.limitations: The article gives a qualitative case description and no prevalence or population denominator for the affected groups.

claims.locator: Publisher body, paragraphs on the vulnerability assessment, project design and project materials arriving in early January 2025.
claims.paraphrase: A locally assessed rainwater system was designed for 134 households (107 Tongariki; 27 Buninga), with raised and reinforced tanks; materials had arrived, but household service was still a future hope.
claims.limitations: Household counts are project design targets; the 2025 account reports materials arriving, not a completed or operating system.

claims.locator: Printed pp. 7–11, policy preamble and ‘Displacement context in Vanuatu’.
claims.paraphrase: The policy treats climate stress, weak governance and urbanization as interacting displacement-risk factors, while separately identifying land conflict and insecure tenure; it says unresolved displacement grievances may contribute to unrest.
institutions: National Advisory Board on Climate Change and Disaster Risk Reduction
claims.limitations: This 2018 policy states conditional, multi-causal risks; it does not establish that climate stress caused a specific conflict event.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: The policy says displacement can contribute to political or social unrest when grievances are not resolved quickly; it names climate change as one influence, not the sole cause.

claims.locator: Printed p. 14, ‘Displacement context in Vanuatu’ and response to repeated flooding.
claims.paraphrase: For communities facing repeated floods, provincial governments sometimes arranged temporary stays with host communities; the policy describes assistance procedures as unclear and responses as ad hoc.
geographies: Vanuatu, repeatedly flooded communities not individually named
claims.limitations: This is a dated policy diagnosis from 2018, not evidence that the coordination gap remains unchanged.

claims.locator: Printed pp. 14–15 and p. 34, including the policy's land-negotiation and community-grievance recommendations.
claims.paraphrase: The policy recommends community-led relocation negotiations, free prior and informed consent of customary landholders, land-dispute grievance channels and host-community support as displacement safeguards.
claims.limitations: These are policy recommendations and safeguards, not verified implementation or outcomes.

claims.locator: Printed pp. 155–157, Vanuatu Community-based Climate Resilience Project, 2024 progress section.
claims.paraphrase: In 2024, 23 of 29 Area Council climate officers were in place; 40 communities developed adaptation plans, while final documentation remained due in 2025.
claims.limitations: Reported outputs, not an impact evaluation.

claims.locator: Printed p. 155, VCCRP external challenges in 2024.
claims.paraphrase: Airline liquidation forced slow, infrequent sea travel to remote targets and disrupted some activities; recruitment and communication also delayed.
geographies: remote VCCRP target communities, not individually named
claims.limitations: The report does not quantify missed activities.

claims.locator: Printed p. 156, VCCRP implementation challenges in 2024.
claims.paraphrase: The Ministry says parliamentary dissolution and political instability disrupted climate-project implementation.
claims.limitations: The report describes no violence and quantifies no delay.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: The Ministry explicitly links political instability to disrupted project implementation.

claims.locator: Printed p. 160, VCCRP 2024 climate-resilient fisheries progress.
claims.paraphrase: Two solar freezers were procured for fisheries cold storage in Mota Lava and Mataso/Makira.

claims.locator: Printed pp. 157–158, VCCRP climate-resilient food preservation progress.
claims.paraphrase: A solar dryer pilot for root crops and vegetables was introduced in Nguna/Pele.

claims.locator: Printed pp. 9–10, Discussion and conclusion; data/method limits at printed p. 3.
claims.paraphrase: For 2012–2020, the pooled Fiji–Solomon Islands–Vanuatu grid-cell analysis found no statistically significant association between climate-disaster shocks or temperature extremes and social-conflict risk.
affected_groups: social groups in three Pacific Island countries
claims.limitations: The pooled result is not a Vanuatu-only estimate; it tests aggregate associations, not mediating mechanisms, and cannot establish that no effects exist.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: The authors report no statistically significant pooled association between disaster shocks or temperature extremes and social-conflict risk in the three-country sample.
claims.source_stated_fcv_locator: Printed pp. 9–10, Discussion; printed p. 3 states that proposed pathways could not be tested.

search_audit.outcome: Read open-access provincial cyclone research and UNDP's Tongariki–Buninga case; North-region climate summary was read but excluded under its written-permission rights notice.

search_audit.query: Vanuatu climate change conflict risk social conflict land displacement policy and climate security evidence
search_audit.outcome: Read a peer-reviewed three-country null-association study and the full 2018 policy's conditional climate, displacement, tenure and grievance pathways; no local causal estimate found.

search_audit.query: Vanuatu political instability climate adaptation project implementation remote community access constraints
search_audit.outcome: The 2024 ministry report explicitly attributes project disruption to political instability and separately reports remote-access constraints; it describes no violence or conflict event.

search_audit.query: Vanuatu local adaptation community resilience water access climate committees fisheries food preservation Area Council reports
search_audit.outcome: The 2024 ministry report documents Area Council officers, community adaptation plans, solar cold storage and a Nguna/Pele solar dryer; the UNDP water-system account remains at project-design/materials stage.

gaps: The ADB multi-hazard assessment for Luganville and a disability-inclusion report were inaccessible (403); indexed material was not used as evidence.
SPREP's linked Van-KIRAP extreme-flood analysis download yielded only its cover, so Port Vila/Luganville flood findings could not be directly checked.
The accessible CSIRO/VMGD Vanuatu North regional climate summary was excluded from findings because its rights notice requires written permission to reproduce or copy material.

No directly read local source established a climate-triggered violent-conflict event. The 2018 policy and pooled research provide conditional and non-detection evidence with the stated limits, not proof of absence.
